findings.location: sections/20-patience-of-the-field.tex lines 257-258 (the Introit paragraph under 'Bearing with one another')
findings.problem: The register repair turned the round-2 sentence 'Because the command and the promise stand in one letter, this interpretation takes the promise to cover the prayer Jerome finds in verse 7' into 'Since the command and the promise stand in one letter, the promise of a hearing covers the prayer for the city that the letter commands.' The study's take has become a deduction about the scope of Jeremias's promise, and the ground given does not carry it. In the letter the hearing of v. 12 follows v. 10 ('When the seventy years shall begin to be accomplished in Babylon, I will visit you ... to bring you again to this place') and leads into the seeking, finding and return of vv. 13-14, while v. 7 gives the prayer for the city its own reason, 'for in the peace thereof shall be your peace.' Jerome, at the locus the second interpretation quotes (In Hier. V on 29:10-14, PL 24 col. 893, read on the page image), glosses 'Tunc invocabitis me, et ibitis Jerusalem: et orabitis, et exaudiam vos' and says that God urges the captives to pray 'ut quod promissum est, mereantur accipere'. In his reading the call that God hears is the prayer for the promised return. The sentence is the Introit's only contribution to this interpretation. It is advisory because it is a single sentence whose ground the reader can see and judge, and the interpretation's argument does not rest on it. The review fragment classes a repair that drops a qualification as a source defect, not a style one.
findings.required_result: The sentence says what the letter does and does not assert that the promise of v. 12 covers the prayer of v. 7. If the extension is kept, it is stated as the study's own and given a ground that carries it. Plain rewrite: 'The same letter that commands this prayer promises a hearing to those who call on God, invocábitis me, et ego exáudiam vos; servants who may not weed the field can still pray for the cockle, asking for the change Augustine's sermon asks of the tares.'

findings.location: sections/30-cry-from-captivity.tex lines 36-37 (the closing sentence of the paragraph 'In the letter the exiles are told to call on God ...')
findings.problem: The repair replaced the labelled sentence 'This interpretation takes the harvest of the parable as a term of the same kind as the letter's seventy years ...' with 'In the parable as in the letter, the one who promises fixes the term and tells those who wait what to do until it comes.' The two preceding sentences already give the letter's term and instruction and the householder's: he 'also tells his servants beforehand what he will do and when ... and until then both are to grow.' The closer restates them as a general formula, and deleting it loses nothing (guidance/editorial.md, 'Each sentence adds something'). The defect is a single instance, so it is advisory.
findings.required_result: The paragraph ends on the householder's words and instruction, or its closing sentence adds something the paragraph has not yet said. Plain rewrite: delete the sentence, so that the paragraph closes on '... and until then both are to grow.'

II, PL 26 cols. 93-94 (own render of PDF p. 54); Chrysostom, Expositio in Ps. 43 sec. 6 (PG 55 Greek OCR, hash-matched), Hom. in Mt. 46.1 and Hom. in Col. 9 (NPNF); Theodoret on Col 3:15-16 (PG 82 Greek OCR) and Theophylact on Col 3:15 (PG 124 col. 1262, Latin OCR), both hash-matched; Rabanus, In Mt. IV, PL 107 col. 947 (tracked OCR); Augustine, Enarr. in Ps. 84.4 and 129.1-3 (NPNF); Bede, In Marc. III on 11:23-25; Douay Jer 29:7-14. Consequential-difficulty tests: (1) Sinite utraque crescere against Auferte malum, Jerome PL 26 cols. 93-94 on the page image: wheat and lolium alike 'quamdiu herba est', 'ne ubi quid ambiguum est, cito sententiam proferamus; sed Deo judicii terminum reservemus', with 1 Cor 5:11 echoed in 'societatem ... cum his qui fratres nominentur'; holds, and 20:24-61 teaches the question and the inference. (2) Why God, having promised, commands prayer: Jerome PL 24 col. 893 on the page image, 'Certe absque invocatione et oratione captivorum, poterat implere Dominus quod promiserat; sed hortatur eos ad preces, ut quod promissum est, mereantur accipere'; holds, taught at 30:39-113. (3) The third interpretation's rebuilt Gradual and Collect links: Chrysostom, PG 55, at Ps 43:7 'when you fight the devil, say: I trust not in my arms', that is not in my strength or my righteousness 'but in the mercy of God', and Hom. in Mt. 46.1 on natural and moral sleep; holds, and 40:48-63 attributes each step correctly. Previous rounds: STU-003 is repaired. Two inference labels remain, one in each of the first and third openings (20:16-17, 40:13-17); every other link of the study's is a plain because, since or so; the five shared-word links of the third interpretation now rest on the text's own content or on a Father's reading of that text, following the round-2 rewrites; all ten texts still contribute in each interpretation; and no rewritten sentence moves the study's inference into a Father's mouth. Advisories STU-017 (a)-(d) and STU-018 are cleared; (a) and (b) were checked in the Greek and Latin. Earlier findings STU-001, 002 and 004-016 stay cleared in the changed paragraphs. New this round: one rewritten sentence drops the round-2 qualification and overstates what Jeremias's promise covers (STU-019); one replacement closer restates its paragraph (STU-020); the manifest and the production record each misstate the study in one place (STU-021). All three are advisory. Verdict PASS: no blocking finding. Limits: no print export was built, so physical extent was not judged; the Greek of PG 55 and PG 82 was read in uncorrected OCR, not on page images; Ambrose, Aquinas, Hilary and the Lasance and 1962 facsimiles were not re-read this round; unchanged prose was read for context and not re-litigated.
